A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PENCIL work. The text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across appendix moves and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original transformer experiments on SAT, QBF and Einstein’s puzzle, including accuracy, reasoning-trace fidelity, inference time and training convergence in Section 4 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix B, including Tables 1–2 and the convergence plots.

M1.justification: The generation/reduction procedure, special tokens, tail-recursion rule and training-loss masking are unchanged. Expanded explanations of summarization and FASP do not introduce a different PENCIL algorithm or model.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SAT and QBF with the same problem-size coverage and Einstein’s puzzles of sizes 3x3, 4x4 and 5x5. No dataset, task or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the direct-answer baseline without CoT, scaffolded CoT and PENCIL. The Einstein’s puzzle, scaling and convergence comparisons retain the same CoT/PENCIL comparator membership.

E3.justification: The 100-instance held-out evaluations, accuracy and trace-rate metrics, model configurations, default 2048-token context and unlimited-context convergence experiment are retained. The FLOPs calculation moves from Section 2.2 to Appendix A without changing the evaluation metric.

E4.justification: The model-size/context-length analysis, scaling and convergence studies, tail-recursion comparison and detailed reasoning examples are retained. Figure 9 moves from Appendix H to Appendix B; the SAT, QBF and Einstein examples are likewise renumbered rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. The retained convergence plots use circles and vertical lines to mark first attainment of optimal performance, not uncertainty.

E6.justification: The numerical tables, empirical plots and appendix examples retain their results. Table 2 still reports 97% PENCIL accuracy versus 25% CoT accuracy on 5x5 puzzles. The existing QBF discrepancy also persists: Section 4.1 says 61% CoT accuracy at n=10, while Table 1 reports 73%.

T1.justification: Definition E.1 revises v1’s Definition C.1 to define FASP as sequence-to-embedding functions, treating token decoding separately and correcting the output-type mismatch with the equivalence theorem. Section 5.1 also drops explicit accepting/rejecting-set disjointness and the infinite-time convention for nonhalting machines. The main simulation theorem and proofs remain unchanged; new Lemma 5.7 restates the existing appendix equivalence result.

C1.justification: The central claims remain context-efficient reasoning, computational savings, strong Einstein’s puzzle performance and Turing-machine simulation with O(T) generated tokens and O(S) context. The rewritten abstract omits the explicit 97% figure, but the introduction and results retain it; the claimed capabilities are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly states that the FASP proof technique can establish other transformer-with-CoT expressiveness results, specifically mentioning Merrill and Sabharwal (2023). This adds a limited applicability claim; the empirical interpretations and model-capacity limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The implementation, data-generation, batching, loss-masking, model and timing information is retained. The same code repository link moves from the experimental section to the introduction, and the relocated FLOPs discussion supplies no new implementation or access information.

R1.justification: Section 6 removes the 'LLMs as Programming Language' paragraph and five associated references, including Tracr and Learning Transformer Programs. It adds an explicit contrast between structured prompting and end-to-end training. FASP’s relationship to RASP becomes more prominent in Section 5.3, although that relationship was already discussed in v1’s Appendix C.

P1.justification: The abstract and Section 5.3 are rewritten, the theoretical overview is streamlined, and related-work paragraphs are reorganized. The FLOPs discussion and supplementary convergence section move earlier in the appendices. These are localized revisions within the retained overall narrative and section structure.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 receive revised spacing, connectors and labels; Figure 1 adds an enclosure around hidden thoughts, and Figure 2’s caption corrects 'blue' highlights to 'green'. Figures 8 and 9 are relocated. The empirical plot designs and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 explains FASP’s role in the proof more clearly and corrects the mismatch between token-output functions and the embedding-function equivalence theorem. These provide a modest gain in accessibility and formal consistency. Removing some programming-language background and explicit conventions in Section 5.1 slightly reduces context and precision, but the main theorem, proof construction and empirical evidence remain intact.
